title: Annealed traffic moderation engine for gradual model rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current rollout primitives (static step lists and percent switches) do not express gradual, metric-driven annealing patterns we want for low-risk model upgrades. We need a policy engine that can express time- and metric-based steps, probabilistic traffic annealing, shadow traffic modes, A/B weighted splits, and automatic rollback/hysteresis guardrails that integrate with Console metrics and Redwood's routing layer.

Goal: Deliver a rollout configuration language + execution engine that: (1) lets PM/Platform define safe progressive exposure patterns, (2) supports both time-based and metric-triggered step progression, (3) inserts shadow traffic for continuous side-by-side evaluation, (4) applies guardrails (latency/error/quality thresholds) and automated rollback, and (5) exposes simulation/dry-run and observability in Console.

Scope: DSL spec, server-side policy compiler and execution runtime, REST API to create rollout policies, integration with metrics adapters (Prometheus/observability pipeline), and Console UI surface for prescriptive templates. Initial implementation will target hosted + dedicated; Private will be supported via compatible control-plane sync and policy export/import.
acceptance_criteria:
- New rollout DSL supports: percent steps, pauses/holds, time windows, metric triggers, and probabilistic annealing curves.
- Execution engine can apply traffic splits and shadow routing without dropping in-flight requests.
- Guardrails evaluate on rolling windows (configurable) and can trigger: hold, rollback, or alert.
- Automatic rollback implements hysteresis to avoid flapping (configurable cool-down and required confirmations).
- Console shows per-rollout telemetry: applied split history, key metrics (P95 latency, error-rate, quality delta), and a dry-run simulator.
- End-to-end test harness demonstrates safe rollback on injected latency and error spikes.
- Performance: policy compile + decision latency < 5ms p95 at 5k RPS policy checks.
design_notes:
- DSL design favors composable primitives: Step(percentage, duration|metricTrigger|probAnneal), Shadow(sampleRate), Guard(metric, operator, threshold, window, action). Provide presets (canary-fast, conservative, annealed-gradual).
- Guard evaluation runs on aggregated rollup metrics; keep decision logic stateless where possible and store progress in a compact persistent store for restarts.
- Probabilistic annealing uses beta-schedule with seedable RNG per deployment to ensure reproducible ramping in test runs.
- Tradeoffs: expressive DSL increases surface area for bugs; provide a strict 'safe' subset for default templates and an 'advanced' mode for power users.
- Security: rollout policy changes require RBAC and an audit trail; tie to existing Console SSO and KMS for policy signing in Private installs.
implementation_plan:
1) Spike (2w): prototype DSL parser and a simulated execution loop against synthetic metrics.
2) Engine MVP (3w): compile DSL -> execution plan, integrate with routing proxy to apply split decisions, implement guard evaluation.
3) Metrics adaptor (2w): integrate with Console ingestion to read P95/err/quality indicators.
4) API + persistence (2w): POST/GET rollout policies, progress checkpoints, and audit logs.
5) Console UI (2w): rollout editor + simulator + telemetry dashboard.
6) E2E tests and perf tuning (2w).
7) Internal rollout -> beta customers -> GA.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: DSL parsing, compile invariants, guard evaluation edge cases.
- Integration tests: fake routing proxy, verify split enforcement, shadow traffic flows, and rollback actions.
- Chaos tests: inject latency/error spikes to trigger guard logic and verify hysteresis prevents flapping.
- Load tests: measure decision latency under 5k/10k RPS policy evaluation scenarios.
- Regression/e2e: run a recorded rollout in dry-run mode and compare telemetry with expected exposure curve.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Internal dogfooding for infra/platform teams (2 weeks) — use conservative preset.
Phase 2: Invite 3 beta customers on Dedicated with support from Solutions Eng.
Phase 3: GA rollout for hosted API and Dedicated; announce templates and docs.
Monitoring: alert for unexpected rollouts, drift between intended vs applied splits, and emergency manual-rollback button in Console.
